output.brief: Pellacott's VA-220 valves built in 2026 are the problem. They are not the installers or the firmware. The lab's matched data shows Pellacott 2026 valves fail at about the same rate (about 41 per 1,000) for legacy and new installers and on firmware 4.1 and 4.2. Durrant-Hale valves stay at 5–7 per 1,000 in every group. In a helium retest of never-installed stock, 11% of Pellacott 2026 valves leaked at the seat. Teardowns show deformed, unseated slide seals. The calibration contractor found the leak rig tagged out of service since January 2026, with no VA-220 test program on any other rig. Certificate tables repeat four fixed sequences, some already in use in 2025. So the "100% leak-tested" certificates look unsupported, and the score rose because it rewards submitted paperwork. I'm quite sure of this. What I can't yet separate is whether the new Corlin seal or the move to Line 3 is the physical cause. Do not release the six held lots on fresh certificates. Quarantine the 2026-built Pellacott stock, suspend dock-to-stock, and run Brenmoor's own helium testing. Drop the installer remediation plan and charge-backs. Raise the matter formally with Pellacott. Then check whether other suppliers' test records are backed by rig logs.
